description: Planted falsifiers. SPEC 18: at least one defect per proof family, and the corresponding checker must fail.

falsifiers.plants: mutated authority bytes
falsifiers.expectedRejector: content digest recomputation

falsifiers.plants: a second copy of the registry's first claim object, spliced verbatim into a COPY of model/claims.json so the planted file is a genuine parser input
falsifiers.expectedRejector: required::registry_violations, the checker `xtask claims list` and `xtask gate` step 2 both call
falsifiers.note: REWRITTEN after a real defect. M2, M3 and M4 each used to reimplement their check inside the falsifier -- M2 appended a duplicate to an in-memory Vec and asserted that dedup shrank it -- so all three tested Rust's standard library and never invoked a gate. The suite reported [PASS] M2 at a moment when model/claims.json genuinely carried two rows with the id UV-004 and `just claims` accepted them. Each now plants its fault in a copy and calls the repository's own checker, with the unmutated copy as a control so it cannot pass by failing for an unrelated reason. Meta-falsified: deleting the duplicate rule from registry_violations turns M2 red and leaves M3 and M4 green.

falsifiers.plants: a dependsOn edge to the claim id GO-999-PLANTED, which does not exist, on a COPY of the registry
falsifiers.expectedRejector: required::registry_violations orphan-dependency rule
falsifiers.note: See M2. Carries the unmutated registry as a control.

falsifiers.plants: a level promotion from `open` to `formalProof` on a claim that has no leanDeclaration -- the exact edit a repository under pressure for a green gate would reach for -- on a COPY of the registry
falsifiers.expectedRejector: required::registry_violations level rule (SPEC 17.1: only formalProof supports 'proved', and a formalProof row with no Lean declaration is that promotion)
falsifiers.note: See M2. Carries the unmutated registry as a control.

falsifiers.plants: sorry on the proof path
falsifiers.expectedRejector: forbidden-construct scan

falsifiers.plants: a compiled-environment response with the exact final release theorem absent
falsifiers.expectedRejector: the exact predicate used by release gate step 9
falsifiers.note: Carries a planted-present control, so the falsifier remains valid after genuine closure.

falsifiers.plants: an exact COPY of WasmGemmGnaf/Atlas/CoverageScope.lean whose real scope-blindness theorem has its required searchPartitions equality replaced by an unrelated declarationBase equality while retaining the real conclusion and proof
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real universalCoverCompleteCheck_scope_blind proof
falsifiers.note: The unmodified CoverageScope source is elaborated first as the control. The mutant attacks the exact dependency used by the theorem's real proof rather than introducing an arbitrary false theorem, and it does not depend on AT-002 remaining absent.

falsifiers.plants: an owned Foundation Lean module added after root generation in a disposable repository, alongside a planted stale WasmGemmGnaf.olean
falsifiers.expectedRejector: the real `xtask sources root --check` source-inventory rejector
falsifiers.note: The same production root generator first creates a control root and `--check` must accept it. The new owned source then makes the root stale even though a compiled-root object is present, and `--check` must reject it. This is independent of the repository's current module count.

falsifiers.plants: a forbidden import (Artifact) into Universal/Competitor.lean
falsifiers.expectedRejector: xtask sources firewall, SPEC 10.1 dependency firewall
falsifiers.note: Guards the property that makes GlobalOptimal meaningful: the competitor universe must be defined without reference to the artifact it will be compared against. Otherwise the theorem is a statement about a universe built around its own answer.

falsifiers.plants: a backward stage-identity binding in a disposable generated MANIFEST.json: sourceManifestCoreIdentity is replaced by the later generatedProofInputIdentity
falsifiers.expectedRejector: the real `xtask manifest --check` identity rejector
falsifiers.note: The production manifest generator creates the control and the production checker must accept it before mutation. The same checker must then reject the backward identity alias. This invokes the release-path rejector instead of locally reimplementing acyclicity over the current manifest.

falsifiers.plants: a weakened GlobalOptimal whose competitor quantifier is restricted by a scope predicate, and -- on a copy of the binding source -- a deleted binding and a tactic-proved one
falsifiers.expectedRejector: the Iff.rfl schema binding in WasmGemmGnaf/Conformance/Schema.lean, and the authority-driven audit in `xtask schema`
falsifiers.note: SPEC 1 requires the gate to compare the compiled UNFOLDED definition against the frozen WGG-GO-1 schema, and says a theorem scoped to a subset of the competitor universe SHALL have a different name. Iff.rfl is what makes that comparison definitional. The falsifier elaborates GlobalOptimalOver <scope> against the same frozen schema and requires it to FAIL, with the unweakened binding as a control so it cannot pass by failing for an unrelated reason. It then attacks the WIRING that decides whether the elaborator is ever asked: on a COPY of Conformance/Schema.lean it deletes the GlobalOptimal binding and, separately, replaces Iff.rfl with `by simp`, and requires `xtask schema` -- whose list of scope-critical definitions is read from the authority JSON, not transcribed -- to report NO BINDING and 'not by definitional reduction' respectively.

falsifiers.plants: a required declaration that is present, correctly named, and choice-tainted
falsifiers.expectedRejector: the SPEC 15 inventory, which reports TAINTED and does not count it as discharged
falsifiers.note: SPEC 4: Classical.choice SHALL NOT produce executable witnesses. A Fintype instance, an enumerator and a decision procedure are DATA, so a choice-tainted closure disqualifies them however well-named they are. An external audit found a name-only check crediting exactly this shape. The planted witness is elaborated against the real compiled environment, so the axiom closure driving the verdict is Lean's own answer; a choice-free witness under the same name is the control and must still be credited.

falsifiers.plants: three mutations of vendor/wasm-spec/SHA256SUMS, each on a COPY of the vendored tree: a flipped hex digit inside a listed digest, an appended line that leaves every per-file digest intact, and a deleted entry
falsifiers.expectedRejector: vendor::binding, the checker `xtask vendor` and release gate step 1 both call
falsifiers.note: SPEC 7.1 says Wasm.profile_matches_pinned_revision means the model and map are identity-bound to the VENDORED revision. Lean cannot read vendor/wasm-spec/; the theorem stands on the literals core3VendorManifestSha256, core3VendoredTree.fileCount and core3RevisionCommit in WasmGemmGnaf/Wasm/Revision.lean, and a literal that had drifted from the tree would still elaborate. The binding is therefore only as good as the checker that recomputes it, and a checker that never fires is indistinguishable from one with nothing to find. The falsifier runs the REAL checker against the planted tree rather than reimplementing it, and carries the unmutated copy as a control so it cannot pass by failing for an unrelated reason. The appended-line mutation is the one that matters most: every per-file digest still checks out, so `sha256sum -c` alone would pass it and only the recorded digest of digests catches it. The repository's own vendored tree is never written.

falsifiers.plants: six independent coverage-integrity attacks against a COPY of the Lean tree: invented opcode, typing-rule, and syntax markers; an attempted covered-count increase; a real marker attached only to comments; and a real marker attached to a declaration absent from the compiled environment
falsifiers.expectedRejector: core::report and core::report_elaborated, the real extracted-checklist checks used by `xtask core`
falsifiers.note: The unmutated copied tree is required to pass first. Invented items must be rejected without increasing the covered count, floating markers must be reported unattached, and a marker above a ghost declaration must be reported unelaborated. The repository itself is never written.

falsifiers.plants: a declaration carrying a required SPEC 15 NAME and the type `Nat`, bound at `:= 0` -- elaborated in a temporary file against the real compiled environment, never in the repository -- plus five wiring attacks: a deleted marker, a `:= @Name` closure replaced by `by exact @Name`, a marker naming something SPEC 15 does not require, an amendment to SPEC.md that leaves a binding's quotation stale, and an exact theorem-shaped prose decoy placed before the drifted fenced theorem
falsifiers.expectedRejector: the `:= @Name` definitional coercion in WasmGemmGnaf/Conformance/RequiredSignatures.lean, and signature::audit plus required::apply_signatures, which `xtask signature`, `xtask claims required` and release gate step 2 all call
falsifiers.note: This is the falsifier for the defect an external audit named directly: 'The repository's reported 36/58 remains inflated. Its checker verifies names rather than exact proposition types; its own M12 test demonstrates that a matching-name `Nat := 0` is counted as discharged.' That was accurate -- `xtask claims required` asked `#print axioms` whether the NAME existed, so any type under that name passed, and M12 planted exactly that shape while only ever testing the choice-taint rule on it. The elaborator half now uses the legitimately exact public-Core `Wasm.decode_sound` binding as its control, plants `Wasm.m15_planted_decode_sound : Nat := 0`, and requires closing the same signature by `:= @<planted>` to fail with a TYPE MISMATCH -- not with an unknown identifier, which would mean the plant never entered the environment and nothing was rejected. The wiring half attacks the checker that decides whether the elaborator is ever asked. In particular, signature::spec_block now reads theorem blocks only from Lean fences; otherwise an exact prose decoy can hide drift in the authoritative fenced proposition. Meta-falsified: emptying required::apply_signatures turns M15 red and leaves M12 green; making signature::closes_definitionally accept everything turns M15 red on its own. Weaker bindings remain machine-readable disclosures and never count as discharge.

falsifiers.plants: two proof-path circularities in the real compiled environment: one forbidden executable theorem cited by a required proof term and one forbidden binary grammar declaration cited by the declarative definition, plus an empty-forbidden control and a required-ledger demotion check
falsifiers.expectedRejector: independence::report_over and required::apply_independence, the real independence and claim-demotion checks
falsifiers.note: The real independence table must first be answerable by the compiled environment. The planted table must identify both known dependencies, the same declarations with no forbidden names must pass, and applying the resulting rejection must move Wasm.decode_sound from discharged to circular. This tests both definition and proof-term inspection without freezing the repository's current repaired/remaining circularity set.

falsifiers.plants: four independent drifts in a COPY of the canonical Core authority-amendment binding: an AMD-005 source digest, an AMD-007 textual anchor, the amended BsN' Lean declaration, and DEV-007's adoptedIntoSpec register edge
falsifiers.expectedRejector: amendment::binding, the real checker used by `xtask amendment` and release-gate step 1
falsifiers.note: The unmutated copied tree is required to pass first. Each plant then calls the real generalized checker, and every modified file is restored before the next plant; the repository itself is never written. This guards all four non-kernel halves of `Wasm.core3AuthorityAmendmentSet`: pinned content, exact textual operation, amended declaration existence, and deviation/amendment registry linkage.

falsifiers.plants: the malformed pinned opcode-275 `I16 X 8` shape in place of AMD-012's corrected `I8 X 16` inserted text, on a COPY of the canonical authority-amendment binding
falsifiers.expectedRejector: amendment::binding, the real checker used by `xtask amendment` and release-gate step 1
falsifiers.note: The unmutated copied tree must pass first. M18 then changes only AMD-012's exact inserted text back to the malformed pinned shape and requires the real digest/anchor/text/deviation binding to reject it. Kernel regressions separately prove that the pinned form has `Instr.wf = false` and the corrected form has `Instr.wf = true`; the mutation guards the non-kernel authority edge selecting the corrected form.

falsifiers.plants: the pinned omission of generalized-supertype `Typeuse_ok` in place of AMD-013's inserted premise, on a COPY of the canonical authority-amendment binding
falsifiers.expectedRejector: amendment::binding, the real checker used by `xtask amendment` and release-gate step 1
falsifiers.note: The unmutated copied tree must pass first. M19 then removes only AMD-013's exact inserted `Typeuse_ok` line, making the recorded insertion a no-op, and requires the real digest/anchor/text/deviation binding to reject it. The kernel counterexample separately demonstrates why the missing premise defeats executable subtype completeness; the mutation guards the non-kernel authority edge selecting the upstream repair.

falsifiers.plants: removal of the exact `TypeGroupRangeOk` conjunct from a COPY of the full amended Core type checker, restoring modulo-2^32 capture of type indices across large recursive groups
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real `ValidateTypes.lean` soundness proof against the declarative `Type_okA` range premise
falsifiers.note: The unmutated copied validator is elaborated first as the control. M20 then removes only the executable non-wrapping group-range check and elaborates the same proof file. The mutant must fail because `checkTypeOkA_sound` can no longer construct `Type_okA`'s source-faithful range premise. This guards the exact defect found while proving finite type-graph origin: `TypeIdx.ofNat` is modulo 2^32, so without the group bound a future recursive-group slot can capture an earlier `_IDX` and invalidate both validation completeness and runtime subtype enumeration.

falsifiers.plants: replacement of the independent lane-store failure-plus-success successor union with a lossy if/else on a COPY of the full amended Core whole-machine successor enumerator
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real `vstoreLaneVal_mem_directSuccessors` completeness proof against the authority `StepA.vstoreLaneVal` rule
falsifiers.note: The pinned lane-store rules deliberately preserve different quantities: the out-of-bounds premise compares `sz` bits while the successful write uses `sz / 8` bytes. Both rules can therefore apply to one state. M21 keeps the unmodified full file as a control, then restores the defective exclusive branch that drops the valid write whenever the broader failure test holds. The real `vstoreLaneVal_mem_directSuccessors` proof then fails, so the mutation detects the lost relational successor rather than merely observing a changed runtime result.

falsifiers.plants: two controlled source-copy mutations: public Wasm.encode in Wasm/CoreBackEnd.lean replaced by ByteArray.empty, and public Artifact.emit in Artifact/Emit.lean replaced by ByteArray.empty
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the actual Wasm.encode_decode_roundtrip and Artifact.decode_emit proof chains
falsifiers.note: Each unmodified full source file is elaborated first as its own control. M22 then changes only the corresponding public encoder implementation and requires the real downstream round-trip proof chain to fail. This guards both the public amended-Core encoder and the chosen-output emitter without claiming byte uniqueness, release selection, GEMM correctness, or a SystemEvaluation.

falsifiers.plants: replacement of the exact public aggregate's moduleBytes = bytes.size conjunct by moduleBytes = 0 on a COPY of Cost/Aggregate.lean while retaining the real module_bytes_exact proof
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the actual Cost.module_bytes_exact projection theorem
falsifiers.note: The unmodified aggregate source is elaborated first as the control. The mutant changes only the byte-accounting conjunct, so rejection demonstrates that the exact theorem is connected to the emitted byte array rather than an unrelated free/static parameter.

falsifiers.plants: replacement of the post-expression state in the public amended global-initializer constructor by its source state on a COPY of Core/InstantiationAmended.lean
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the actual GC-state-threading witness and public amended initializer relation
falsifiers.note: The unmodified amended initializer is elaborated first as the control. M24 then restores only the pinned same-state `Eval_expr` premise in `EvalGlobalsA.cons`; the real heap-persistence proof must fail because `struct.new` and `array.new*` append managed-heap instances. This guards AMD-014's kernel-facing state-threading edge rather than merely checking the amendment record.

falsifiers.plants: removal of the exact no-rebased-`REC` suffix conjunct from a COPY of the amended recursive-type checker, restoring the pinned mixed `Rectype_ok/cons` then `_rec2` scope reset
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real `ValidateTypes.lean` soundness proof against AMD-015's `Rectype_okA/cons` premise
falsifiers.note: The unmodified validator is elaborated first as the control. M25 then removes only the executable suffix-scope check from the ordinary-cons arm. The real soundness proof must fail because it can no longer construct the amended declarative premise. A separate kernel counterexample preserves the pinned mixed derivation and shows it derives `NOFUNC <: STRUCT` although every heap-decision fuel returns false.

falsifiers.plants: replacement of the public costed-reduction constructor's exact erased event by a different Harness initialization event on a COPY of Wasm/Evaluate.lean, where the public CostedReduces and its structural erasure proof are defined
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real public CostedReduces erasure proof and costed_erase_iff_plain_run theorem
falsifiers.note: The unmodified public erasure module is elaborated first as the control. M26 then changes only the event consumed by CostedReduces.cons while leaving CostedEvent.erase unchanged; the structural erasure proof must fail because a charged transition no longer projects to the authority trace it claims.

falsifiers.plants: deletion of the public compiler's mandatory private-status-local epilogue from a COPY of GNAF/Compile.lean while retaining the real lowering equation
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of GNAF.bodyCode_has_status_epilogue in the full copied compiler source
falsifiers.note: The unmodified direct amended-Core compiler is elaborated first as the control. M27 then changes the actual bodyCode lowering, not a fixture or expected output, by deleting its final private-status-local read. The kernel-checked source equation must cease to elaborate, guarding BI-001/BI-010's real public compile target against an ABI-changing lowering edit.

falsifiers.plants: replacement of the canonical public evaluator equation in SystemEvaluationRel by a reflexive completed-result equation on a COPY of Universal/Evaluate.lean
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real Universal.system_evaluation_rel_sound reflection proof
falsifiers.note: The unmodified executable evaluator is elaborated first as the control. The mutant makes every supplied SystemEvaluation satisfy the relation without running decoding, validation, input enumeration, or execution. The real soundness proof must then fail because it can no longer derive ProfileValid from the relation equation.

falsifiers.plants: removal of the amended float-literal syntax-well-formedness premise from the full-width load rule on a COPY of the public amended-Core execution/successor proof chain
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real byte-decoder completeness and mem_successors_iff_step proof against the amended read relation
falsifiers.note: The unmodified execution and successor sources are elaborated first as the control. M29 then makes the amended load-num-val premise vacuous while retaining the real proof that every relational target is the single canonical decoded literal. The mutant must fail on the kernel-checked malformed-F32 collision witnessed by DEV-016; changing a fixture or expected runtime output is insufficient.

falsifiers.plants: replacement of the canonical public costed-explorer call in a COPY of Universal/Evaluate.lean by an unconditional initialization-failure result
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real execution_checker_complete_within_sublevel and system_evaluation_rel_complete proofs
falsifiers.note: The unmodified executable evaluator is elaborated first as the control. M30 then disconnects its per-input checker from Wasm.exploreAllCosted while retaining the real completeness proofs. The mutant must fail because semantic correctness and the no-overrun resource premise can no longer produce a completed input or system evaluation; changing a fixture or an expected output is insufficient.

falsifiers.plants: replacement of the Harness raw-install target page count by one page fewer on a COPY of Core/HarnessExecution.lean
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real growMemoryForRaw_splice_available theorem against the mutated growth computation
falsifiers.note: The unmodified Harness source is elaborated first as the control. M31 then changes the actual target used by the raw-install transition from `requiredPages(ptr+len)` to one page short while retaining the kernel proof that a successful growth makes the complete splice window available. The mutant must fail on a page-boundary invocation; changing a fixture or an expected cost is insufficient. M30 is reserved for the independent Universal proof family.

falsifiers.plants: replacement of AMD-018's `ValType.nvb` implicit-select operand tests by `ValType.isNumOrVec` on a COPY of the sole full amended checker
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real `Validate.unreachable_select_checkSeqA` theorem, stated beside the production `checkInstrA` in Wasm/Core/ValidateInstr.lean
falsifiers.note: The unmodified full checker/completeness source is elaborated first as the control. M32 then restores only the pre-amendment implicit-select test. The real two-instruction `[unreachable, select none]` theorem must fail because polymorphic pops infer `BOT`, which the amended declarative rule admits below its numeric/vector witness. The mutation changes the production checker, not a fixture or expected output.

falsifiers.plants: removal of AMD-019's executable-candidate equality premise from the public Harness `InitializesA` constructor on a COPY of the initialization/successor proof chain
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real `Harness.InitializesA.target_functional` and `Wasm.mem_successors_iff_step` proofs
falsifiers.note: The unmodified Harness initialization boundary is elaborated first as the control. M33 then removes only the equality that excludes a reflexively terminal indexed `ref.null`, while retaining the kernel counterexample and real target-functionality/successor proofs. The mutant must fail because the relation again admits both the raw indexed-null target and the closed target selected by `Step_read/ref.null-idx`; changing an evaluator fixture is insufficient.

falsifiers.plants: two independent mutations on copies of the production Harness execution module: `GemmFunctionReady` replaced by `True`, and `RawInstallReady` replaced by `True`
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real missing-function and missing-memory-zero refutations and the positive readiness extraction theorems
falsifiers.note: The unmodified Harness execution source is elaborated first as the control. Each mutant removes one computed ABI-readiness check while leaving the real theorems that extract its executable content in place. The callable mutant must fail because `True` cannot yield a selected function instance; the raw-install mutant must fail because `True` cannot yield an `installRaw? = some ...` result. This attacks the production predicates, not a fixture, stored progress conclusion, or expected runtime output.

falsifiers.plants: removal of AMD-021's `Valtype_okA` premise from both constructors of the production `Local_okA` relation on a COPY of the amended module-validation source
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real `Local_okA.valtype_ok` extraction and out-of-range reference-local rejection theorem
falsifiers.note: The unmodified amended module relation is elaborated first as the control. M35 removes only the two local value-type validity premises while retaining the pinned counterexample and the production theorems that extract validity and reject it. The mutant must fail because defaultability alone admits a non-null reference local whose type index is absent from the context. This attacks the sole amended relation, not a fixture or an expected Boolean.

falsifiers.plants: removal of AMD-022's operative `REC i <: STRUCT` constructor from a COPY of the production amended heap-subtyping relation
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the production `Heaptype_subA.rec_struct_any` REC-shape coherence theorem and downstream rolled-type/full-validator proof chain
falsifiers.note: The unmodified amended subtyping source is elaborated first as the control. M36 removes only the exact stored-STRUCT REC-shape constructor while retaining the production theorem that composes it through STRUCT and EQ to ANY. The mutant must fail at that real semantic bridge; ARRAY and FUNC rules, declared-super edges, and fixtures are unchanged.

falsifiers.plants: removal of the production scalar compiler's `setStatus` assignment from a COPY of the complete source-to-Core status simulation module
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real `DirectScalar.apply_statusAssignments` source/lowering correspondence theorem
falsifiers.note: The unmodified scalar runtime bridge is elaborated first as the control. M37 changes the operative status-assignment extraction, not an expected result or proof fixture, while retaining the theorem that equates it with the independent Plan.supportedStatus semantics. The mutant must fail because a checked setStatus plan would otherwise return a different status from its source evaluation.

falsifiers.plants: increment of the production compiler execution-cost dispatch coordinate from five to six on a COPY of the exact cost module
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of `DirectScalarCost.compose_formula_eq_certifiedCost` against the independent CheckedPlan.certifiedCost definition
falsifiers.note: The unmodified cost-reflection module is elaborated first as the control. M38 changes one real execution-cost coordinate while leaving the independently defined source formula and the coordinatewise composition proof untouched. The mutant must fail at the exact formula bridge; no expected output, evaluator result, or theorem statement is edited.

falsifiers.plants: removal of AMD-023's operative event-labelled handler-body context constructor from a COPY of the repaired Core execution/progress proof chain
falsifiers.expectedRejector: Lean elaboration of the real handler structural-progress bridge and exact public `Wasm.validation_progress` theorem
falsifiers.note: The unmodified repaired execution and public progress sources are elaborated first as the control. M39 then removes only the operative `StepA.ctxtHandler` constructor (and its exact event arm) while retaining the production theorem that lifts an inner handler-body step and the full public progress proof. The mutant must fail on the claim-specific validated/reachable handler witness pinned by `handler_validation_progress_counterexample`; deleting a stored witness, changing an expected result, or weakening the public carrier is insufficient.

note: A mutation suite that merely expects runtime output differences does not test universal-coverage integrity (SPEC 18). M4 and M6 target claim integrity directly.
